thread:
emily.design: quick design huddle — want UX + a11y eyes on the compact trace selection and export copy. two specific asks:
1) microcopy for export CTA (we need something clear for mixed audiences)
2) keyboard focus / screen reader behavior for correlation pill + stackframe links

raj.prod: for (1) do we prefer verbs (Download/Export) or nouns (Snapshot/Archive)? i lean verbs bc action clarity.

lina.a11y: verbs are usually better for buttons — "Download trace snapshot" reads clear, but long. consider primary CTA: "Download" and a secondary descriptive line: "Trace snapshot (JSON)". also keyboard focus/order thoughts below.

matt.eng: implementation note — export currently streams a .json blob. short primary label ("Download") is easiest, but we should preserve context near the button so users know what they're downloading. can't add multi-line labels inside button without breaking layout.

emily.design: ok proposal: primary button = "Download"; small help text under button: "Download trace snapshot (JSON, includes spans & events)". also want the correlation pill to be keyboard reachable before the export button when in drilldown. current tab order jumps to actions first.

lina.a11y: tab order should follow visual reading order: correlation pill -> timeline -> actions. For screen readers, the correlation pill should have an aria-label like `aria-label=\"Correlation ID: 9f3b... — open related requests\"` and a role of button if it opens a modal. add `aria-live=\"polite\"` announcements when export completes: e.g., "Trace snapshot downloaded" or "Download failed".

accessibility-bot: automated note: before rollout, run axe-core check and manual VoiceOver / NVDA pass on export flow.

matt.eng: technical: adding aria-live will be trivial. the pill currently is an anchor; turning into a button for better semantics ok but may need small routing tweaks. the timeline is a canvas (svg) so keyboard focus currently lands on the wrapper div — we'll add tabindex=0 and a short skip link to jump into the timeline.

emily.design: about microcopy variants — options we debated: 1) "Download trace snapshot" (explicit), 2) "Export trace" (shorter, more technical), 3) "Save snapshot" (ambiguous). Lina, which is best for screen reader clarity?

lina.a11y: #1 wins for clarity in assistive tech. If UI constraints demand shorter label, use "Download" + visible helper text (not aria-hidden) that reads: "Trace snapshot (JSON)". Also: ensure link text in stackframe list includes function name and short file:line to avoid contextless links in VO list.

raj.prod: thumbs up for #1 too. also suggest adding a tiny icon (download) to the button for visual affordance — keep alt text empty and use aria-hidden on decorative svg.

emily.design: decision: primary CTA = "Download"; helper line = "Trace snapshot (JSON, includes spans & events)"; correlation pill = role=\"button\" with `aria-label` including the id and action; add `aria-live=\"polite\"` for download success/failure. Add tabindex fixes and a skip link for timeline. i'll update figma and write a JIRA for eng with these specifics.

matt.eng: i'll pick up the JIRA. quick question — for the helper line, should it be visible text or visually-hidden aria text? visible is better for discoverability.

lina.a11y: visible helper text is best. make it small and low-contrast but still meets 3:1 contrast for readability.

emily.design: ok final tasks:
- emily: update Figma and copy tokens
- matt: JIRA to convert pill to button, add aria-label, aria-live, tabindex fixes, and helper text placement
- lina: add test cases (NVDA/VoiceOver) and acceptance criteria in the JIRA

emily.design: thanks all — will ping once mock is updated. :thumbsup:
